entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pope Zephyrinus, the bishop of Rome from 199 to 217, played a pivotal role in shaping the early Christian Church's response to heresies and defending the divinity of Christ.

Born in Rome, Zephyrinus succeeded Victor I as bishop and continued his predecessor's efforts to combat false teachings and maintain orthodoxy.

During his papacy, Zephyrinus also oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries, particularly in Rome and North Africa.

His legacy extends to the later Church Fathers, who would build upon his work in their own debates about theology and doctrine.

"The Church is the pillar and foundation of truth," Zephyrinus once said, "and it is the guardian of the truth," demonstrating his commitment to upholding the Church's teachings.
